decisions.reason: Babylon was famous for its learned men, who read omens, the stars and dreams and gave counsel to the king (51:57; Isaiah 47:13; Daniel 2:2). Their wisdom will not save the city.

decisions.choice: princes (L), officials (B), leaders (R); Chaldeans (L, B), Babylonians (R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for these words. Readable adds the verb "strike" to the chant and repeats it.

decisions.choice: ¡Espada contra ...!
decisions.reason: Verses 35-38 repeat "sword" (*ḥerev*) five times and end with "drought" (*ḥorev*), a play on sound; Literal and Balanced keep the repeated cry.

source.text: חֶ֥רֶב אֶל־הַבַּדִּ֖ים וְנֹאָ֑לוּ חֶ֥רֶב אֶל־גִּבּוֹרֶ֖יהָ וָחָֽתּוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: [A] sword against the empty talkers, and they will become fools; [a] sword against her warriors, and they will be shattered.

en.L: A sword against the empty talkers, and they will become fools! \q A sword against her warriors, and they will be shattered!
en.B: A sword against the babblers, so that they become fools! \q A sword against her warriors, so that they are shattered!
en.R: A sword will strike the false prophets, and they will look like fools. \q A sword will strike its soldiers, and they will be broken and terrified.

es.L: ¡Espada contra los charlatanes, y se volverán necios! \q ¡Espada contra sus valientes, y serán quebrantados!
es.B: ¡Espada contra los habladores, para que se vuelvan necios! \q ¡Espada contra sus guerreros, para que sean destrozados!
es.R: La espada herirá a los falsos profetas, y quedarán como necios. \q La espada herirá a sus soldados, y quedarán destrozados y aterrados.

fr.L: L’épée contre les bavards, et ils deviendront fous ! \q L’épée contre ses guerriers, et ils seront brisés !
fr.B: L’épée contre les beaux parleurs, et ils perdront la raison ! \q L’épée contre ses guerriers, et ils seront brisés !
fr.R: L’épée frappera les faux prophètes, et ils passeront pour des fous. \q L’épée frappera ses soldats, et ils seront brisés et terrifiés.

sw.L: Upanga juu ya wapiga domo, nao watakuwa wapumbavu! \q Upanga juu ya mashujaa wake, nao watavunjika!
sw.B: Upanga dhidi ya wabwabwajaji, ili wawe wapumbavu! \q Upanga dhidi ya mashujaa wake, ili wavunjwevunjwe!
sw.R: Upanga utawapiga manabii wa uongo, nao wataonekana wapumbavu. \q Upanga utawapiga askari wake, nao watavunjika na kuogopa.

vi.L: Gươm nghịch cùng những kẻ nói khoác, và chúng sẽ hóa ngu dại! \q Gươm nghịch cùng các dũng sĩ của nó, và chúng sẽ bị đập tan!
vi.B: Gươm nghịch cùng những kẻ ba hoa, để chúng hóa ra ngu dại! \q Gươm nghịch cùng các dũng sĩ của nó, để chúng bị đập tan!
vi.R: Gươm sẽ đánh các tiên tri giả, và chúng sẽ trở nên ngu dại. \q Gươm sẽ đánh quân lính của nó, và chúng sẽ tan vỡ và khiếp sợ.

decisions.choice: the empty talkers: those who speak lies as omens
decisions.reason: The word means idle talk, and so those who talk it: here the diviners and omen-readers of Babylon, as in Isaiah 44:25. Their predictions will be shown to be empty.

decisions.choice: they will become fools: they will be shown up as foolish
decisions.reason: The verb means to be or to act foolishly (5:4; Isaiah 19:13). Events will prove that their words had no meaning.

decisions.choice: shattered: broken and in terror
decisions.reason: As in verse 2, the verb means both to be shattered and to be broken by fear.

decisions.choice: empty talkers (L), babblers (B), false prophets (R); broken and terrified (R)
decisions.reason: The wording of Isaiah 44:25 for the same word. Readable gives both sides of the verb "shattered" (meaning decision m3).

source.text: חֶ֜רֶב אֶל־סוּסָ֣יו וְאֶל־רִכְבּ֗וֹ וְאֶל־כָּל־הָעֶ֛רֶב אֲשֶׁ֥ר בְּתוֹכָ֖הּ וְהָי֣וּ לְנָשִׁ֑ים חֶ֥רֶב אֶל־אוֹצְרֹתֶ֖יהָ וּבֻזָּֽזוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: [A] sword against her horses and against her chariots and against all the mixed people who [are] in her midst, and they will become women; [a] sword against her treasures, and they will be plundered.

en.L: A sword against her horses and against her chariots, and against all the mixed people who are in her midst, and they will become women! \q A sword against her treasures, and they will be plundered!
en.B: A sword against her horses and her chariots and against all the mixed peoples in her midst, so that they become like women! \q A sword against her treasures, so that they are looted!
en.R: A sword will strike its horses and its chariots and all the foreigners in the city. They will lose their courage and be afraid. \q A sword will strike its treasures, and they will be carried away.

es.L: ¡Espada contra sus caballos y contra sus carros, y contra toda la mezcla de gente que está en medio de ella, y serán como mujeres! \q ¡Espada contra sus tesoros, y serán saqueados!
es.B: ¡Espada contra sus caballos y sus carros, y contra toda la gente mezclada que hay en ella, para que se vuelvan como mujeres! \q ¡Espada contra sus tesoros, para que sean saqueados!
es.R: La espada herirá a sus caballos y a sus carros, y a todos los extranjeros que hay en la ciudad. Perderán el valor y tendrán miedo. \q La espada herirá sus tesoros, y se los llevarán.

fr.L: L’épée contre ses chevaux et contre ses chars, et contre tout le ramassis de peuples qui est au milieu d’elle, et ils deviendront des femmes ! \q L’épée contre ses trésors, et ils seront pillés !
fr.B: L’épée contre ses chevaux et ses chars, et contre tous les étrangers qui vivent au milieu d’elle, et ils deviendront comme des femmes ! \q L’épée contre ses trésors, et ils seront pillés !
fr.R: L’épée frappera ses chevaux, ses chars et tous les étrangers de la ville. Ils perdront courage et auront peur. \q L’épée frappera ses trésors, et ils seront emportés.

sw.L: Upanga juu ya farasi wake na juu ya magari yake ya vita, na juu ya watu wote wa mchanganyiko walio katikati yake, nao watakuwa wanawake! \q Upanga juu ya hazina zake, nazo zitatekwa nyara!
sw.B: Upanga dhidi ya farasi wake na magari yake ya vita, na dhidi ya watu wote wa mataifa mchanganyiko walio kati yake, ili wawe kama wanawake! \q Upanga dhidi ya hazina zake, ili zitekwe nyara!
sw.R: Upanga utawapiga farasi wake, magari yake ya vita na wageni wote walio mjini. Watapoteza ujasiri wao na kuogopa. \q Upanga utazipiga hazina zake, nazo zitachukuliwa.

vi.L: Gươm nghịch cùng ngựa của nó, nghịch cùng xe chiến của nó, và nghịch cùng mọi dân pha tạp ở giữa nó, và chúng sẽ trở nên như đàn bà! \q Gươm nghịch cùng các kho báu của nó, và chúng sẽ bị cướp đoạt!
vi.B: Gươm nghịch cùng ngựa và xe chiến của nó, và nghịch cùng mọi dân pha tạp ở giữa nó, để chúng trở nên như đàn bà! \q Gươm nghịch cùng các kho báu của nó, để chúng bị cướp sạch!
vi.R: Gươm sẽ đánh ngựa và xe chiến của nó, và mọi người ngoại quốc trong thành. Chúng sẽ mất hết can đảm và sợ hãi. \q Gươm sẽ đánh các kho báu của nó, và chúng sẽ bị cướp đi.

decisions.choice: the mixed people: foreigners living in Babylon, perhaps hired soldiers
decisions.reason: The word names people of many origins living among a nation (25:20, 24; Exodus 12:38). In Babylon they may be the foreign troops who fought for the city, as the horses and chariots before them suggest, or the foreign residents of verse 16.

decisions.choice: they will become women: they will lose all courage
decisions.reason: In the speech of the time, to say that soldiers become women was to say that they lose heart and cannot fight (51:30; Isaiah 19:16; Nahum 3:13). It describes their terror, not the worth of women.

decisions.choice: her treasures: the same word as "armory" in verse 25
decisions.reason: The word means a storehouse or treasury. God opens his own storehouse of weapons (verse 25), and Babylon's storehouses are plundered.

decisions.choice: like women (B); They will lose their courage and be afraid (R); foreigners (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced says "like women", since the picture is a comparison. Readable says what it means (meaning decision m2) and uses a plain word for the mixed people.

decisions.choice: "watakuwa wanawake" (L), "wawe kama wanawake" (B); Readable "Watapoteza ujasiri wao"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew picture of soldiers who "become women" means that they lose all courage; Literal and Balanced keep it, Readable says what it means, as the English does.

source.text: חֹ֥רֶב אֶל־מֵימֶ֖יהָ וְיָבֵ֑שׁוּ כִּ֣י אֶ֤רֶץ פְּסִלִים֙ הִ֔יא וּבָאֵימִ֖ים יִתְהֹלָֽלוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: [A] drought against her waters, and they will dry up; for [a] land of carved images it [is], and over [the] terrors they act madly.

en.L: A drought against her waters, and they will dry up! \q For it is a land of carved images, \q and they go mad over terrors.
en.B: A drought on her waters, so that they dry up! \q For it is a land of idols, \q and they are crazed by their dreadful images.
en.R: A drought will come on its waters, and they will dry up. \q For Babylon is a land full of idols, \q and its people have gone crazy over these frightening statues.

es.L: ¡Sequía sobre sus aguas, y se secarán! \q Porque es tierra de imágenes talladas, \q y enloquecen por sus horrores.
es.B: ¡Sequía sobre sus aguas, para que se sequen! \q Porque es una tierra de ídolos, \q y se vuelven locos por sus imágenes espantosas.
es.R: Vendrá una sequía sobre sus aguas, y se secarán. \q Porque Babilonia es una tierra llena de ídolos, \q y su gente se ha vuelto loca por esas estatuas que dan miedo.

fr.L: La sécheresse contre ses eaux, et elles tariront ! \q Car c’est un pays d’images sculptées, \q et ils perdent la tête pour des épouvantails.
fr.B: La sécheresse sur ses eaux, et elles tariront ! \q Car c’est un pays d’idoles, \q et ils sont fous de leurs images terrifiantes.
fr.R: La sécheresse frappera ses eaux, et elles tariront. \q Car Babylone est un pays plein d’idoles, \q et ses habitants sont devenus fous de ces statues effrayantes.

sw.L: Ukame juu ya maji yake, nayo yatakauka! \q Kwa maana ni nchi ya sanamu za kuchonga, \q nao wanaenda wazimu kwa ajili ya vitisho.
sw.B: Ukame juu ya maji yake, ili yakauke! \q Kwa maana ni nchi ya sanamu, \q nao wamerukwa na akili kwa sababu ya sanamu zao za kutisha.
sw.R: Ukame utakuja juu ya maji yake, nayo yatakauka. \q Kwa maana Babeli ni nchi iliyojaa sanamu, \q nao watu wake wamerukwa na akili kwa ajili ya sanamu hizo za kutisha.

vi.L: Hạn hán nghịch cùng các dòng nước nó, và chúng sẽ khô cạn! \q Vì đó là một xứ đầy tượng chạm, \q và chúng điên cuồng vì những hình tượng ghê sợ.
vi.B: Hạn hán giáng trên các dòng nước nó, để chúng khô cạn! \q Vì đó là xứ của các thần tượng, \q và chúng mê cuồng vì các hình tượng đáng sợ.
vi.R: Hạn hán sẽ đến trên các dòng nước của nó, và chúng sẽ khô cạn. \q Vì Ba-by-lôn là một xứ đầy thần tượng, \q và dân nó điên cuồng vì những pho tượng đáng sợ ấy.

decisions.choice: a drought: a play on "sword"
decisions.reason: The word for drought is written with the same letters as the word for sword in verses 35-37; only the vowels differ. With the vowels of the text, the chant ends with a wordplay: after five swords, a drought. Some read the same letters as "sword" here too, continuing the series. The vowels of the text are followed.

decisions.choice: her waters: the Euphrates and the canals
decisions.reason: Babylon stood on the Euphrates, and its fields and its defenses depended on the river and a network of canals (51:13, 36; Isaiah 44:27). Without water the city could neither live nor be defended.

decisions.choice: carved images ... terrors: idols, mocked as frightening things
decisions.reason: The first word means images carved from wood or stone (8:19; 51:47). The second means terrors or dreadful things (Exodus 15:16); here it is a scornful name for idols, which frighten their worshipers but have no power. Its use for idols is found only here.

decisions.choice: they go mad: they act like people out of their minds
decisions.reason: The verb is used of people raving like madmen, drunk on the cup of God's anger (25:16; 51:7). Babylon's devotion to its idols is a kind of madness.

decisions.choice: idols ... dreadful images (B); idols ... frightening statues (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the carved images as idols and say what the "terrors" are (meaning decision m3).

source.text: לָכֵ֗ן יֵשְׁב֤וּ צִיִּים֙ אֶת־אִיִּ֔ים וְיָ֥שְׁבוּ בָ֖הּ בְּנ֣וֹת יַֽעֲנָ֑ה וְלֹֽא־תֵשֵׁ֥ב עוֹד֙ לָנֶ֔צַח וְלֹ֥א תִשְׁכּ֖וֹן עַד־דּ֥וֹר וָדֽוֹר׃

records.literal_gloss: Therefore will dwell desert creatures with hyenas, and will dwell in her daughters of [the] ostrich, and not she will be inhabited again forever, and not she will be settled to generation and generation.

en.L: Therefore desert creatures will dwell with hyenas, \q and ostriches will dwell in her; \q she will never again be inhabited, \q nor will she be settled from generation to generation.
en.B: So desert creatures will live there with hyenas, \q and ostriches will make their home in her. \q She will never be lived in again, \q nor settled through all generations.
en.R: So wild animals of the desert and hyenas will live there. \q Ostriches will live in Babylon. \q No people will ever live there again, \q not for all time to come.

es.L: Por eso habitarán [allí] fieras del desierto con hienas, \q y habitarán en ella avestruces; \q nunca más será habitada, \q ni será poblada de generación en generación.
es.B: Por eso vivirán allí fieras del desierto junto con hienas, \q y los avestruces harán en ella su morada. \q Nunca más será habitada, \q ni poblada por todas las generaciones.
es.R: Por eso vivirán allí animales salvajes del desierto y hienas. \q Los avestruces vivirán en Babilonia. \q Nunca más vivirá gente allí, \q por todos los tiempos.

fr.L: C’est pourquoi les bêtes du désert habiteront avec les hyènes, \q et les autruches habiteront en elle ; \q elle ne sera plus jamais habitée, \q ni peuplée de génération en génération.
fr.B: Alors les bêtes du désert y vivront avec les hyènes, \q et les autruches y feront leur demeure. \q Elle ne sera plus jamais habitée, \q ni peuplée au fil des générations.
fr.R: Alors les animaux sauvages du désert et les hyènes vivront là. \q Les autruches habiteront à Babylone. \q Plus personne n’y vivra jamais, \q pour toujours.

sw.L: Kwa hiyo wanyama wa nyikani watakaa pamoja na fisi, \q na mbuni watakaa ndani yake; \q hatakaliwa tena milele, \q wala hatakaliwa kizazi baada ya kizazi.
sw.B: Kwa hiyo wanyama wa jangwani wataishi huko pamoja na fisi, \q na mbuni watafanya makao ndani yake. \q Hatakaliwa na watu tena kamwe, \q wala hatakaliwa katika vizazi vyote.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo wanyama wa porini wa jangwani na fisi wataishi huko. \q Mbuni wataishi Babeli. \q Hakuna watu watakaoishi huko tena kamwe, \q hata milele.

vi.L: Vì vậy các thú hoang sa mạc sẽ ở với linh cẩu, \q và đà điểu sẽ ở trong đó; \q nó sẽ không bao giờ có người ở nữa, \q cũng không có ai cư ngụ từ đời này sang đời kia.
vi.B: Vì thế thú hoang sa mạc sẽ sống ở đó với linh cẩu, \q và đà điểu sẽ làm tổ trong đó. \q Nó sẽ không bao giờ có người ở nữa, \q cũng không ai định cư ở đó đời đời.
vi.R: Vì thế thú hoang sa mạc và linh cẩu sẽ sống ở đó. \q Đà điểu sẽ sống tại Ba-by-lôn. \q Sẽ không bao giờ còn ai sống ở đó nữa, \q mãi mãi về sau.

decisions.choice: desert creatures, hyenas, ostriches: wild animals of waste places
decisions.reason: The same animals live in the ruins of Babylon in Isaiah 13:21-22 and of Edom in Isaiah 34:13-14. The first word means creatures of dry places. The second is probably the hyena, though it may be the jackal. "Daughters of the ostrich" is a usual name for the ostrich, though some take it as an owl. The point is that only wild animals will live there.

decisions.choice: never inhabited from generation to generation: as in Isaiah 13:20
decisions.reason: Isaiah spoke of Babylon in the same way: it will never be lived in, from generation to generation (Isaiah 13:20).

decisions.choice: wild animals of the desert; not for all time to come
decisions.reason: Readable uses a plain phrase for the desert creatures and for "generation and generation".

source.text: כְּמַהְפֵּכַ֨ת אֱלֹהִ֜ים אֶת־סְדֹ֧ם וְאֶת־עֲמֹרָ֛ה וְאֶת־שְׁכֵנֶ֖יהָ נְאֻם־יְהוָ֑ה לֹֽא־יֵשֵׁ֥ב שָׁם֙ אִ֔ישׁ וְלֹֽא־יָג֥וּר בָּ֖הּ בֶּן־אָדָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: As [the] overthrow [by] God of Sodom and Gomorrah and her neighbors, declares Yahweh, not will dwell there [a] man, and not will sojourn in her [a] son of man.

en.L: As when God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah and their neighbors, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q no one will live there, \q and no {{gender:human being|son of man}} will sojourn in it.
en.B: As when God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah and the towns near them, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q no one will live there; \q no human being will settle in it.
en.R: Babylon will be like Sodom and Gomorrah and the towns near them when God destroyed them, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q No one will live there. \q No one will even stay there for a while.

es.L: Como cuando Dios destruyó a Sodoma y a Gomorra y a sus vecinas, declara {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, \q no habitará allí nadie, \q ni residirá en ella {{gender:ningún ser humano|hijo de hombre}}.
es.B: Como cuando Dios destruyó a Sodoma y Gomorra y a las ciudades vecinas, afirma {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, \q nadie vivirá allí; \q ningún ser humano se establecerá en ella.
es.R: Babilonia quedará como Sodoma y Gomorra y las ciudades vecinas cuando Dios las destruyó, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}. \q Nadie vivirá allí. \q Nadie se quedará allí ni siquiera por un tiempo.

fr.L: Comme lorsque Dieu bouleversa Sodome et Gomorrhe et leurs voisines, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, \q personne n’y habitera, \q et aucun {{gender:être humain|fils d’homme}} n’y séjournera.
fr.B: Comme lorsque Dieu bouleversa Sodome, Gomorrhe et les villes voisines, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, \q personne n’y habitera ; \q aucun être humain ne s’y installera.
fr.R: Babylone sera comme Sodome, Gomorrhe et les villes voisines quand Dieu les a détruites, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}. \q Personne n’y habitera. \q Personne n’y restera même pour un temps.

sw.L: Kama Mungu alipoipindua Sodoma na Gomora na jirani zake, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, \q hakuna mtu atakayekaa huko, \q wala mwanadamu hatakaa ndani yake kama mgeni.
sw.B: Kama Mungu alipoipindua Sodoma na Gomora na miji iliyokuwa karibu nayo, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, \q hakuna mtu atakayeishi huko; \q hakuna mwanadamu atakayekaa ndani yake.
sw.R: Babeli itakuwa kama Sodoma na Gomora na miji iliyokuwa karibu nayo Mungu alipoiangamiza, anasema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. \q Hakuna mtu atakayeishi huko. \q Hakuna mtu hata atakayekaa huko kwa muda.

vi.L: Như khi Đức Chúa Trời lật đổ Sô-đôm, Gô-mô-rơ và các thành lân cận, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán vậy, \q sẽ không ai ở đó, \q không con người nào sẽ trú ngụ trong đó.
vi.B: Như khi Đức Chúa Trời hủy diệt Sô-đôm, Gô-mô-rơ và các thành lân cận, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán vậy, \q sẽ không ai sống ở đó; \q không một người nào sẽ định cư tại đó.
vi.R: Ba-by-lôn sẽ giống như Sô-đôm, Gô-mô-rơ và các thành lân cận khi Đức Chúa Trời hủy diệt chúng, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán. \q Không ai sống ở đó. \q Thậm chí không ai dừng chân ở đó.

decisions.choice: the overthrow of Sodom and Gomorrah: the pattern of total destruction
decisions.reason: God's destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah (Genesis 19:24-25) became the picture of a judgment that leaves nothing behind (Deuteronomy 29:22; Amos 4:11; Isaiah 13:19, of Babylon). The same words are said of Edom in 49:18, except that here God is named as the one who overthrew the cities and the LORD "declares" rather than "says".

decisions.choice: stay: live as a sojourner, for a time
decisions.reason: The second verb means to live somewhere as a guest or newcomer. Not only will no one settle there; no one will even stop there.

decisions.choice: a man ... a son of man: any human being
decisions.reason: Both phrases mean any person at all, as in 49:18 and 49:33.

decisions.choice: human being (L, with the gender setting; B)
decisions.reason: The words mean any person, men and women alike, so Literal uses the gender setting with the traditional wording "son of man" as the alternative. The two lines keep the wording of 49:18 at each level, where the Hebrew is the same; Readable puts the comparison into its own sentence.

decisions.choice: the wording of 49:18
decisions.reason: The same saying as of Edom, kept in the same words.

decisions.choice: the wording of 49:18 at each level, with no gender span on "mwanadamu"
decisions.reason: The same words were said of Edom; "mwanadamu" already means any human being.

source.text: הִנֵּ֛ה עַ֥ם בָּ֖א מִצָּפ֑וֹן וְג֤וֹי גָּדוֹל֙ וּמְלָכִ֣ים רַבִּ֔ים יֵעֹ֖רוּ מִיַּרְכְּתֵי־אָֽרֶץ׃

records.literal_gloss: Look, [a] people coming from [the] north, and [a] nation great and kings many will be stirred up from [the] remotest parts of [the] earth.

en.L: Look, a people is coming from the north, \q and a great nation and many kings \q will be stirred up from the farthest parts of the earth.
en.B: See, an army is coming from the north; \q a mighty nation and many kings \q are being roused from the ends of the earth.
en.R: Look! An army is coming from the north. \q A powerful nation and many kings are getting ready to fight. \q They are coming from far away.

es.L: He aquí, un pueblo viene del norte, \q y una nación grande y muchos reyes \q se levantan de los confines de la tierra.
es.B: Un ejército viene del norte; \q una nación poderosa y muchos reyes \q se ponen en marcha desde los extremos de la tierra.
es.R: ¡Atención! Un ejército viene del norte. \q Una nación poderosa y muchos reyes se preparan para la guerra. Vienen de muy lejos.

fr.L: Voici, un peuple vient du nord, \q et une grande nation et de nombreux rois \q se lèvent des extrémités de la terre.
fr.B: Voici qu’une armée vient du nord ; \q une nation puissante et de nombreux rois \q se lèvent du bout de la terre.
fr.R: Regardez ! Une armée arrive du nord. \q Une nation puissante et de nombreux rois se préparent à combattre. \q Ils viennent de très loin.

sw.L: Tazama, watu wanakuja kutoka kaskazini, \q na taifa kubwa na wafalme wengi \q wataamshwa kutoka pande za mbali za dunia.
sw.B: Tazama, jeshi linakuja kutoka kaskazini; \q taifa kuu na wafalme wengi \q wanaamshwa kutoka miisho ya dunia.
sw.R: Tazama! Jeshi linakuja kutoka kaskazini. \q Taifa lenye nguvu na wafalme wengi wanajiandaa kupigana. \q Wanatoka mbali sana.

vi.L: Kìa, một dân đang đến từ phương bắc, \q một dân tộc lớn và nhiều vua \q sẽ được khích động từ tận cùng trái đất.
vi.B: Kìa, một đạo quân đang đến từ phương bắc; \q một dân tộc hùng mạnh và nhiều vua \q đang được khích động từ tận cùng trái đất.
vi.R: Hãy xem! Một đạo quân đang đến từ phương bắc. \q Một dân tộc hùng mạnh và nhiều vua đang sửa soạn giao chiến. \q Họ đến từ nơi rất xa.

decisions.choice: 6:22-24 turned against Babylon
decisions.reason: Verses 41-43 repeat 6:22-24, where an army from the north came against Zion; now the same words announce an army from the north against Babylon. The differences in this verse: there is no "Thus says the LORD" before it, the people come "from the north" rather than "from the land of the north", and "many kings" are added to the great nation.

decisions.choice: many kings: the allied rulers of the attacking army
decisions.reason: The Persian empire that took Babylon was made up of many peoples, each with its rulers; 51:27-28 names the kings of the Medes and the kingdoms of Ararat, Minni and Ashkenaz.

decisions.choice: the wording of 6:22, with the changes
decisions.reason: Each level keeps its wording of 6:22 where the Hebrew is the same, so the reader can hear the repetition, and adds "many kings". As there, Balanced and Readable say "an army" for "a people".

decisions.choice: the wording of 6:22
decisions.reason: Verses 41-43 turn against Babylon the words once spoken against Zion (6:22-24), and the Spanish of that passage is reused at each level. Changes follow the Hebrew: "from the north" for "from the land of the north", "and many kings", "daughter of Babylon" for "daughter of Zion", the king of Babylon for "we", and "they are cruel" (plural) in verse 42.

decisions.choice: the Swahili wording of 6:22-24 at each level, reused for 50:41-43
decisions.reason: The oracle against Zion in 6:22-24 is turned against Babylon here; the same Swahili lets a reader hear it, and only what the Hebrew changes is changed: "and many kings", "they are cruel", "daughter Babylon", and the king of Babylon who hears instead of "we".

decisions.choice: verses 41-43 repeat 6:22-24
decisions.reason: The Hebrew of 6:22-24 is said again against Babylon; the French keeps the wording of 6:22-24 at each level and changes only what the Hebrew changes ("from the north", "and many kings", "they are cruel", "daughter of Babylon", "the king of Babylon ... him").

decisions.choice: the wording of 6:22-24 at each level
decisions.reason: Verses 41-43 repeat 6:22-24 against Babylon, and the Vietnamese of 6:22-24 is kept at each level. It changes only where the Hebrew does: no "CHÚA phán" opening, "từ phương bắc" for "từ xứ phương bắc", "và nhiều vua" added, "chúng tàn bạo" for "nó tàn bạo", "ngươi, hỡi con gái Ba-by-lôn" for "con gái Si-ôn", and the king of Babylon ("vua") in place of "chúng tôi" in verse 43.

source.text: קֶ֣שֶׁת וְכִידֹ֞ן יַחֲזִ֗יקוּ אַכְזָרִ֥י הֵ֨מָּה֙ וְלֹ֣א יְרַחֵ֔מוּ קוֹלָם֙ כַּיָּ֣ם יֶהֱמֶ֔ה וְעַל־סוּסִ֖ים יִרְכָּ֑בוּ עָר֗וּךְ כְּאִישׁ֙ לַמִּלְחָמָ֔ה עָלַ֖יִךְ בַּת־בָּבֶֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: Bow and javelin they grasp; cruel [are] they, and not they have mercy; their sound like the sea roars, and on horses they ride, arrayed like a man for battle against you, daughter of Babylon.

en.L: They grasp bow and javelin; \q they are cruel, and they have no mercy; \q their sound roars like the sea, \q and they ride on horses, \q arrayed like a man for battle against you, daughter of Babylon.
en.B: They take hold of bow and spear; \q they are cruel and show no mercy. \q The noise of them roars like the sea \q as they ride on horses, \q lined up like a warrior for battle against you, Daughter Babylon.
en.R: Their soldiers carry bows and spears. \q They are cruel and do not show mercy. \q They ride horses, and they sound like the roaring sea. \q They are lined up, ready to fight against you, people of Babylon.

es.L: Empuñan arco y jabalina; \q crueles son, y no tienen compasión; \q su estruendo ruge como el mar, \q y montan a caballo, \q dispuestos como un solo hombre para la guerra contra ti, hija de Babilonia.
es.B: Empuñan arco y lanza; \q son crueles y no tienen piedad. \q Su estruendo ruge como el mar \q mientras cabalgan en sus caballos, \q formados como un guerrero para la batalla contra ti, hija de Babilonia.
es.R: Sus soldados llevan arcos y lanzas. \q Son crueles y no tienen compasión. \q Montan a caballo, y suenan como el mar cuando ruge. \q Están formados, listos para pelear contra ti, pueblo de Babilonia.

fr.L: Ils saisissent l’arc et le javelot ; \q ils sont cruels, et ils n’ont pas de pitié ; \q leur voix mugit comme la mer, \q et ils montent des chevaux, \q rangés comme un seul homme pour le combat contre toi, fille de Babylone.
fr.B: Ils empoignent l’arc et la lance ; \q ils sont cruels et sans pitié. \q Leur bruit gronde comme la mer, \q tandis qu’ils chevauchent, \q rangés comme un guerrier pour la bataille contre toi, fille de Babylone.
fr.R: Leurs soldats portent des arcs et des lances. \q Ils sont cruels et n’ont aucune pitié. \q Ils montent à cheval, et leur bruit est comme le grondement de la mer. \q Ils sont en rang, prêts à combattre contre toi, peuple de Babylone.

sw.L: Wanashika upinde na mkuki; \q wao ni wakatili, wala hawana huruma; \q sauti yao inanguruma kama bahari, \q nao wanapanda farasi, \q wamejipanga kama mtu wa vita dhidi yako, binti Babeli.
sw.B: Wanashika upinde na mkuki; \q ni wakatili, wala hawana huruma. \q Kelele zao zinanguruma kama bahari \q wakipanda farasi, \q wamejipanga kama shujaa wa vita dhidi yako, Binti Babeli.
sw.R: Askari wao wanabeba pinde na mikuki. \q Ni wakatili, wala hawana huruma. \q Wanapanda farasi, na sauti yao ni kama ya bahari inayonguruma. \q Wamejipanga tayari kupigana nanyi, enyi watu wa Babeli.

vi.L: Chúng cầm cung và lao; \q chúng tàn bạo và không có lòng thương xót; \q tiếng của chúng gầm như biển cả, \q và chúng cưỡi trên ngựa, \q dàn trận như một người ra chiến đấu nghịch cùng ngươi, hỡi con gái Ba-by-lôn.
vi.B: Chúng nắm chặt cung và giáo; \q chúng tàn bạo và không chút thương xót. \q Tiếng của chúng gầm vang như biển cả \q khi chúng cưỡi ngựa kéo đến, \q dàn trận như một chiến binh để đánh ngươi, hỡi con gái Ba-by-lôn.
vi.R: Binh lính chúng mang cung và giáo. \q Chúng tàn ác và không chút thương xót. \q Chúng cưỡi ngựa, và tiếng của chúng như biển gầm thét. \q Chúng đã dàn quân sẵn sàng đánh ngươi, hỡi dân Ba-by-lôn.

decisions.choice: as 6:23, with "daughter of Babylon" for "daughter of Zion"
decisions.reason: The verse repeats 6:23. Two things change: "they are cruel" stands for "it is cruel", and the army now comes against Daughter Babylon instead of Daughter Zion. The cruelty Babylon showed Zion is turned back on itself.

decisions.choice: arrayed like a man for battle: drawn up as one warrior
decisions.reason: As in 6:23, the whole army stands in its ranks as if it were one man ready to fight.

decisions.choice: daughter of Babylon: the city pictured as a young woman
decisions.reason: The city and its people are spoken of as a daughter, as Zion is (Isaiah 47:1, 5). The tender name makes her fall more pitiful.

decisions.choice: the wording of 6:23; Daughter Babylon (B), people of Babylon (R)
decisions.reason: Each level keeps its wording of 6:23, changing only what the Hebrew changes. "Daughter Babylon" follows the settled "Daughter Zion", and Readable says "people of Babylon" as it says "people of Zion".

decisions.choice: "binti Babeli" (L); "Binti Babeli" (B); "watu wa Babeli" (R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for daughter Babylon in Swahili, as Psalm 137:8.

decisions.choice: "fille de Babylone" (L, B); "peuple de Babylone" (R)
decisions.reason: As the French terms note sets it (Psalm 137:8).

decisions.choice: con gái Ba-by-lôn (L, B); dân Ba-by-lôn (R)
decisions.reason: Daughter Babylon as the terms note sets it, after Psalm 137:8.

source.text: שָׁמַ֧ע מֶֽלֶךְ־בָּבֶ֛ל אֶת־שִׁמְעָ֖ם וְרָפ֣וּ יָדָ֑יו צָרָה֙ הֶחֱזִיקַ֔תְהוּ חִ֖יל כַּיּוֹלֵדָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Has heard [the] king of Babylon their report, and dropped his hands; distress has seized him, anguish like [a woman] giving birth.

en.L: The king of Babylon has heard the report of them, and his hands have dropped; \q distress has seized him, \q anguish like [a woman] giving birth.
en.B: The king of Babylon has heard the news of them; his hands hang limp; \q distress has gripped him, \q pain like a woman in labor.
en.R: The king of Babylon has heard about this army. He has no strength left. \q He is terrified. \q He hurts like a woman giving birth to a baby.

es.L: El rey de Babilonia ha oído su fama, y se han debilitado sus manos; \q la angustia se ha apoderado de él, \q dolor como de [mujer] que da a luz.
es.B: El rey de Babilonia ha oído la noticia, y sus manos cuelgan sin fuerza; \q la angustia lo ha atrapado, \q dolores como de mujer de parto.
es.R: El rey de Babilonia ha oído hablar de ese ejército. Ya no le quedan fuerzas. \q Está aterrado. \q Le duele como a una mujer que está dando a luz.

fr.L: Le roi de Babylone en a entendu la nouvelle, et ses mains ont faibli ; \q la détresse l’a saisi, \q une douleur comme [celle d’une femme] qui enfante.
fr.B: Le roi de Babylone a appris la nouvelle, et ses mains sont sans force ; \q l’angoisse l’a pris, \q une douleur comme celle d’une femme en travail.
fr.R: Le roi de Babylone a entendu parler de cette armée. Il n’a plus de force. \q Il est terrifié. \q Il a mal comme une femme qui met un enfant au monde.

sw.L: Mfalme wa Babeli amesikia habari zao; mikono yake imelegea; \q dhiki imemshika, \q utungu kama wa [mwanamke] anayezaa.
sw.B: Mfalme wa Babeli amesikia habari zao, na mikono yake imelegea; \q dhiki imemshika, \q maumivu kama ya mwanamke mwenye utungu.
sw.R: Mfalme wa Babeli amesikia habari za jeshi hili. Hana nguvu tena. \q Amejawa na hofu. \q Anaumia kama mwanamke anayezaa mtoto.

vi.L: Vua Ba-by-lôn đã nghe tin về chúng; tay vua rã rời; \q sự khốn quẫn đã bắt lấy vua, \q cơn đau đớn như [người đàn bà] sinh nở.
vi.B: Vua Ba-by-lôn đã nghe tin về chúng, và tay vua bủn rủn; \q nỗi khốn quẫn đã siết lấy vua, \q cơn đau như người đàn bà đang chuyển dạ.
vi.R: Vua Ba-by-lôn đã nghe về đạo quân ấy. Vua chẳng còn chút sức lực nào. \q Vua kinh hoàng. \q Vua đau đớn như người đàn bà sinh con.

decisions.choice: as 6:24, with the king of Babylon in place of the people of Zion
decisions.reason: In 6:24 the people of Jerusalem said, "We have heard the report of it; our hands have dropped." Now the king of Babylon hears the news and his hands drop. The panic Babylon caused comes on its own king.

decisions.choice: his hands have dropped: all strength and courage are gone
decisions.reason: As in 6:24, hands that hang down are a picture of helpless fear (Isaiah 13:7).

decisions.choice: anguish like a woman giving birth: sudden pain that cannot be escaped
decisions.reason: As in 6:24, the terror of war is compared to the pains of childbirth (Isaiah 13:8).

decisions.choice: the wording of 6:24, with "he" for "we"
decisions.reason: Each level keeps its wording of 6:24 and changes only the speaker, as the Hebrew does. As there, Readable explains the dropping hands and names the distress as fear.

source.text: הִ֠נֵּה כְּאַרְיֵ֞ה יַעֲלֶ֨ה מִגְּא֣וֹן הַיַּרְדֵּן֮ אֶל־נְוֵ֣ה אֵיתָן֒ כִּֽי־אַרְגִּ֤עָה אֲרִיצֵם֙ מֵֽעָלֶ֔יהָ וּמִ֥י בָח֖וּר אֵלֶ֣יהָ אֶפְקֹ֑ד כִּ֣י מִ֤י כָמ֨וֹנִי֙ וּמִ֣י יוֹעִדֶ֔נִּי וּמִֽי־זֶ֣ה רֹעֶ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר יַעֲמֹ֖ד לְפָנָֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: Look, like [a] lion [that] comes up from [the] thicket of the Jordan to [a] pasture ever-flowing, for in [a] moment I will make them run from upon her, and whoever [is] chosen over her I will appoint; for who [is] like me, and who will summon me, and who [is] this shepherd who will stand before me?

en.L: Look, like a lion he comes up from the thicket of the Jordan \q to an ever-flowing pasture; \q for in an instant I will make them run from her, \q and whoever is chosen I will appoint over her. \q For who is like {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and who will summon {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}? \q And who is this shepherd who can stand before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}?
en.B: Look, an enemy will come up like a lion from the thick brush along the Jordan \q against the pastures that never run dry. \q In an instant I will chase Babylon's people from their land, \q and I will set over it the one I choose. \q For who is like {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}? Who can call {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to account? \q What shepherd can stand against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}?
en.R: An enemy will come like a lion out of the thick bushes along the Jordan River \q to attack sheep in their green fields. \q In a moment I will chase the people of Babylon out of their land. \q Then I will put the one I choose in charge of it. \q No one is like {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. No one can challenge {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. \q No ruler can stand up against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

es.L: He aquí, como león sube de la espesura del Jordán \q a la pradera siempre verde; \q porque en un instante los haré correr de ella, \q y al que sea escogido pondré sobre ella. \q Porque ¿quién es como yo, y quién {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} emplazará? \q ¿Y quién es el pastor que podrá estar delante de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}?
es.B: He aquí que un enemigo subirá como un león desde la espesura del Jordán \q contra los pastos que nunca se secan. \q En un instante echaré de su tierra a la gente de Babilonia, \q y pondré sobre ella al que yo elija. \q Porque ¿quién es como yo? ¿Quién {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} puede pedir cuentas? \q ¿Qué pastor puede hacer{{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} frente?
es.R: Un enemigo vendrá como un león desde los matorrales espesos junto al río Jordán \q para atacar a las ovejas en sus prados verdes. \q En un momento echaré de su tierra a la gente de Babilonia. \q Luego pondré a cargo de ella al que yo elija. \q Nadie es como yo. Nadie {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} puede desafiar. \q Ningún gobernante puede hacer{{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} frente.

fr.L: Voici, comme un lion il monte des fourrés du Jourdain \q vers un pâturage toujours vert ; \q car en un instant je les en ferai fuir, \q et celui qui est choisi, je l’établirai sur elle. \q Car qui est comme {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, et qui {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} citera en justice ? \q Et qui est ce berger qui tiendra devant {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} ?
fr.B: Voici qu’un ennemi monte comme un lion des fourrés du Jourdain \q contre les pâturages qui ne tarissent jamais. \q En un instant, je chasserai les habitants de Babylone de leur pays, \q et j’y établirai celui que je choisirai. \q Car qui est comme {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} ? Qui peut {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} demander des comptes ? \q Quel berger peut tenir tête devant {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} ?
fr.R: Un ennemi va sortir comme un lion des épais buissons du bord du Jourdain \q pour attaquer les moutons dans leurs prés verts. \q En un instant, je chasserai les gens de Babylone de leur pays. \q Puis je mettrai à sa tête celui que je choisirai. \q Personne n’est comme {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}. Personne ne peut {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} défier. \q Aucun chef ne peut {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} résister.

sw.L: Tazama, kama simba anapanda kutoka katika vichaka vya Yordani \q mpaka malisho ya daima; \q kwa maana mara moja nitawafanya wakimbie kutoka kwake, \q na yeye aliyechaguliwa nitamweka juu yake. \q Kwa maana ni nani aliye kama {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}, na ni nani atakayeniita mahakamani? \q Na ni nani mchungaji huyo awezaye kusimama mbele {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}?
sw.B: Tazama, adui atapanda kama simba kutoka katika vichaka vizito kando ya Yordani \q dhidi ya malisho yasiyokauka kamwe. \q Mara moja nitawafukuza watu wa Babeli kutoka katika nchi yao, \q nami nitamweka juu yake yule nitakayemchagua. \q Kwa maana ni nani aliye kama {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}? Ni nani awezaye kunihoji? \q Ni mchungaji gani awezaye kusimama dhidi {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}?
sw.R: Adui atakuja kama simba kutoka katika vichaka vizito kando ya Mto Yordani \q kuwashambulia kondoo katika malisho yao mabichi. \q Mara moja nitawafukuza watu wa Babeli kutoka katika nchi yao. \q Kisha nitamweka yule nitakayemchagua kuwa msimamizi wake. \q Hakuna aliye kama {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}. Hakuna awezaye kunipinga. \q Hakuna mtawala awezaye kusimama dhidi {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}.

vi.L: Này, như sư tử nó đi lên từ bụi rậm sông Giô-đanh \q đến đồng cỏ xanh tươi quanh năm; \q vì trong chốc lát {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ khiến chúng chạy khỏi nó, \q và ai được chọn {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ lập trên nó. \q Vì ai giống như {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, ai sẽ đòi {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} ra hầu tòa? \q Kẻ chăn nào có thể đứng trước mặt {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}?
vi.B: Này, như sư tử, quân thù sẽ từ bụi rậm dọc sông Giô-đanh đi lên \q đánh những đồng cỏ không bao giờ khô cạn. \q Trong chốc lát {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ đuổi dân Ba-by-lôn khỏi xứ họ, \q và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ lập người {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} chọn cai trị xứ ấy. \q Vì ai giống như {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}? Ai dám bắt {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} phải giải trình? \q Kẻ chăn nào có thể chống lại {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}?
vi.R: Quân thù sẽ đến như sư tử ra khỏi bụi rậm dọc sông Giô-đanh \q để tấn công đàn chiên trên đồng cỏ xanh. \q Trong chốc lát {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ đuổi dân Ba-by-lôn ra khỏi xứ họ. \q Rồi {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ đặt người {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} chọn cai quản xứ ấy. \q Không ai giống như {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. Không ai có thể thách thức {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. \q Không người lãnh đạo nào có thể đứng lên chống lại {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.

decisions.choice: like a lion he will come up: the attacker God sends
decisions.reason: The one who comes up like a lion is not named. In this verse he is most likely the conqueror God sends against Babylon, whom God then appoints over it. Some take the lion to be God himself, who speaks in the next words (25:38; Hosea 5:14).

decisions.choice: the thicket of the Jordan: the dense growth along the river, where lions lived
decisions.reason: The banks of the Jordan were thick with bushes and reeds, where lions had their lairs (12:5; Zechariah 11:3).

decisions.choice: a pasture that never fails: a settled, well-watered home
decisions.reason: The second word means lasting or ever-flowing, used of a stream that never runs dry. The pasture is Babylon, secure and at ease, with its flocks, its people, in it. The lion falls on them there.

decisions.choice: repeats 49:19 (of Edom)
decisions.reason: Verses 44-46 repeat 49:19-21, said there of Edom, with Babylon in its place. In this verse the people are "them" where 49:19 has "him". The written text and the reading the scribes marked for reading aloud spell "I will make them run" slightly differently, with the same meaning.

decisions.choice: who will summon me ... what shepherd can stand before me: no one can challenge God
decisions.reason: To summon is to call someone to court or to set a time for a contest (Job 9:19). The shepherd is a ruler, as in verse 6. No king or court can call God to account or resist him.

decisions.choice: the wording of 49:19 at each level
decisions.reason: Each level keeps the wording of 49:19, changing only what the Hebrew changes (m4): "them" and "her" for Edom's "him" and "it". As there, Balanced and Readable name the one who comes up as an enemy and the people chased away as Babylon's, and Readable turns the questions, which expect the answer "no one", into statements and says "ruler" for "shepherd".

decisions.choice: the wording of 49:19
decisions.reason: The saying about Edom returns against Babylon, in the same words at each level, with Babylon in place of Edom.

decisions.choice: the wording of 49:19 at each level, with Babylon for Edom
decisions.reason: The verse repeats the oracle on Edom; each level keeps its wording there and changes only what the Hebrew changes.

decisions.choice: the French wording of 49:19 at each level, with Babylon for Edom
decisions.reason: Verses 44-46 repeat 49:19-21 of Babylon; the French keeps the same wording, changing only what the Hebrew changes.

decisions.choice: the wording of 49:19 at each level
decisions.reason: Verses 44-46 repeat 49:19-21 against Babylon; the Vietnamese reuses that wording and changes only what the Hebrew changes.

source.text: לָכֵ֞ן שִׁמְע֣וּ עֲצַת־יְהוָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֤ר יָעַץ֙ אֶל־בָּבֶ֔ל וּמַ֨חְשְׁבוֹתָ֔יו אֲשֶׁ֥ר חָשַׁ֖ב אֶל־אֶ֣רֶץ כַּשְׂדִּ֑ים אִם־לֹ֤א יִסְחָבוּם֙ צְעִירֵ֣י הַצֹּ֔אן אִם־לֹ֥א יַשִּׁ֛ים עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם נָוֶֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Therefore hear [the] plan of Yahweh which he has planned against Babylon and his purposes which he has purposed against [the] land of [the] Chaldeans: surely they will drag them away, [the] little ones of the flock; surely will be appalled over them [their] pasture.

en.L: Therefore hear the plan of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has planned against Babylon, \q and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} purposes that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has purposed against the land of the Chaldeans: \q surely they will drag them away, the little ones of the flock; \q surely [their] pasture will be appalled over them.
en.B: So hear the plan {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has made against Babylon, \q the purposes {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has formed against the land of the Chaldeans: \q even the little ones of the flock will be dragged away; \q their pasture will be appalled at their fate.
en.R: So listen to what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has planned against Babylon. \q Listen to what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has decided to do to the land of the Babylonians. \q Even the youngest lambs of the flock will be dragged away. \q Even their pasture will be shocked at what happens to them.

es.L: Por tanto, {{plural_you:oigan|oíd}} el plan {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} ha trazado contra Babilonia, \q y {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} designios que ha decidido contra la tierra de los caldeos: \q ciertamente los arrastrarán, a los pequeños del rebaño; \q ciertamente [su] pastizal quedará espantado por ellos.
es.B: Por eso {{plural_you:escuchen|escuchad}} el plan que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ha trazado contra Babilonia, \q los designios que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} ha formado contra la tierra de los caldeos: \q hasta los pequeños del rebaño serán arrastrados; \q su pastizal quedará espantado por su suerte.
es.R: Así que {{plural_you:escuchen|escuchad}} lo que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ha planeado contra Babilonia. \q {{plural_you:Escuchen|Escuchad}} lo que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} ha decidido hacer a la tierra de los babilonios. \q Hasta los corderitos del rebaño serán arrastrados. \q Hasta sus prados se espantarán de lo que les pase.

fr.L: C’est pourquoi, écoutez le dessein {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a conçu contre Babylone, \q et {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} projets qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a projetés contre le pays des Chaldéens : \q oui, on les traînera, les petits du troupeau ; \q oui, [leur] pâturage sera consterné à leur sujet.
fr.B: Écoutez donc le plan que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a formé contre Babylone, \q les projets qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a conçus contre le pays des Chaldéens : \q même les petits du troupeau seront traînés au loin ; \q leur pâturage sera consterné de leur sort.
fr.R: Écoutez donc ce que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a prévu contre Babylone. \q Écoutez ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a décidé de faire au pays des Babyloniens. \q Même les plus jeunes agneaux du troupeau seront emmenés de force. \q Même leurs prés seront choqués de ce qui leur arrive.

sw.L: Kwa hiyo sikieni shauri la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alilolipanga juu ya Babeli, \q na makusudi {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} aliyoyakusudia juu ya nchi ya Wakaldayo: \q hakika watawaburuta, wadogo wa kundi; \q hakika malisho [yao] yatashangaa juu yao.
sw.B: Basi sikieni mpango ambao {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ameupanga dhidi ya Babeli, \q makusudi aliyoyaweka dhidi ya nchi ya Wakaldayo: \q hata wadogo wa kundi watakokotwa mbali; \q malisho yao yatashangaa kwa yale yatakayowapata.
sw.R: Basi sikilizeni yale {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliyoyapanga dhidi ya Babeli. \q Sikilizeni yale aliyoamua kuitendea nchi ya Wababeli. \q Hata wana-kondoo wadogo kabisa wa kundi watakokotwa mbali. \q Hata malisho yao yatashtuka kwa yale yatakayowapata.

vi.L: Vì vậy hãy nghe kế hoạch của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} mà {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã định nghịch cùng Ba-by-lôn, \q và các ý định của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} mà {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã định nghịch cùng xứ của người Canh-đê: \q chắc chắn chúng sẽ bị kéo đi, những con nhỏ nhất của bầy; \q chắc chắn đồng cỏ [của chúng] sẽ kinh hãi vì chúng.
vi.B: Vậy hãy nghe kế hoạch {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã định nghịch cùng Ba-by-lôn, \q những ý định {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã hoạch định nghịch cùng xứ của người Canh-đê: \q ngay cả những con nhỏ nhất trong bầy cũng sẽ bị kéo đi; \q đồng cỏ của chúng sẽ kinh hãi về số phận của chúng.
vi.R: Vậy hãy nghe điều {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã định nghịch cùng Ba-by-lôn. \q Hãy nghe điều {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã quyết định làm cho xứ của người Ba-by-lôn. \q Ngay cả những chiên con nhỏ nhất trong bầy cũng sẽ bị kéo đi. \q Ngay cả đồng cỏ của chúng cũng sẽ bàng hoàng trước điều xảy đến cho chúng.

decisions.choice: surely ...: the form of an oath
decisions.reason: "If not" at the start of a line is the shortened form of an oath: it means "surely", "I swear it will be so" (15:11; 49:20).

decisions.choice: the little ones of the flock: even the weakest
decisions.reason: The young of the flock are its weakest members. Even they will be dragged off, as by beasts of prey. Some take the phrase as "the shepherd boys", the least of the shepherds.

decisions.choice: their pasture will be appalled at them: their home will be left in horror
alternatives: he will make their pasture desolate
decisions.reason: The verb means to be appalled, and also to be made desolate. The pasture, the people's home, is pictured as stunned at what happens to them. It can also be read as "he will make their pasture desolate because of them".

decisions.choice: repeats 49:20 (of Edom)
decisions.reason: The verse repeats 49:20 with Babylon and the land of the Chaldeans in place of Edom and the people of Teman.

decisions.choice: even the little ones ... will be dragged away (B); youngest lambs (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable keep the wording of 49:20 where the Hebrew is the same, and give the oath form's force with "even" and make the dragging passive, since its subject is not named.

decisions.choice: the wording of 49:20
decisions.reason: Kept as in the oracle against Edom, with Babylon and the Chaldeans in place of Edom and Teman.

source.text: מִקּוֹל֙ נִתְפְּשָׂ֣ה בָבֶ֔ל נִרְעֲשָׁ֖ה הָאָ֑רֶץ וּזְעָקָ֖ה בַּגּוֹיִ֥ם נִשְׁמָֽע׃ס

records.literal_gloss: From [the] sound of "has been seized Babylon" quakes the earth, and [a] cry among the nations is heard.

en.L: At the sound of "Babylon has been seized!" \q the earth quakes, \q and a cry is heard among the nations.
en.B: At the shout, "Babylon is taken!" \q the earth will shake, \q and a cry will be heard among the nations.
en.R: When people hear that Babylon has been captured, \q the earth will shake. \q The nations will hear people crying out.

es.L: Al grito de «¡Tomada es Babilonia!» \q tiembla la tierra, \q y se oye clamor entre las naciones.
es.B: Al grito de «¡Babilonia ha caído!» \q la tierra temblará, \q y se oirá un clamor entre las naciones.
es.R: Cuando la gente oiga que Babilonia ha sido conquistada, \q la tierra temblará. \q Las naciones oirán los gritos de la gente.

fr.L: Au bruit de « Babylone a été prise ! » \q la terre tremble, \q et un cri s’entend parmi les nations.
fr.B: Au cri de « Babylone est prise ! » \q la terre tremblera, \q et une clameur s’entendra parmi les nations.
fr.R: Quand on apprendra que Babylone a été prise, \q la terre tremblera. \q Les nations entendront des cris.

sw.L: Kwa sauti ya "Babeli imetwaliwa!" \q nchi inatetemeka, \q na kilio kinasikika kati ya mataifa.
sw.B: Kwa sauti ya, "Babeli imetekwa!" \q nchi inatikisika, \q na kilio kinasikika kati ya mataifa.
sw.R: Watu watakaposikia kwamba Babeli imetekwa, \q dunia itatetemeka. \q Mataifa yatasikia watu wakilia.

vi.L: Nghe tiếng "Ba-by-lôn đã bị chiếm!" \q đất rúng động, \q và tiếng kêu la vang lên giữa các dân tộc.
vi.B: Nghe tiếng hô: "Ba-by-lôn đã bị chiếm!" \q đất sẽ rung chuyển, \q và tiếng kêu la sẽ vang lên giữa các dân tộc.
vi.R: Khi người ta nghe tin Ba-by-lôn đã bị chiếm, \q đất sẽ rung chuyển. \q Các dân tộc sẽ nghe tiếng người ta kêu la.

decisions.choice: repeats 49:21 (of Edom), with a change at the end
decisions.reason: In 49:21 the earth quakes at the sound of Edom's fall, and the cry is heard at the Red Sea. Here it is Babylon's capture, and the cry is heard among the nations. The whole world feels the fall of the great power (51:54).

decisions.choice: has been seized: the cry that goes up
decisions.reason: The verb is the same as in verse 24. The words "Babylon has been seized" are the news that is shouted, as in verse 2.

decisions.choice: the earth quakes: the world shaken by Babylon's fall
decisions.reason: The earth trembling is a picture of the shock of great events (8:16; Isaiah 14:16; Ezekiel 26:15).

decisions.choice: will shake ... will be heard (B, R)
decisions.reason: The verbs speak of the coming fall as done; Balanced and Readable put them in the future, which English uses for what is still to come. Readable says the news in plain words.
